title: Hamburger Kunsthalle re-evaluates Modernism Collection in major new exhibition
summary: THIS IS THE MODERN WORLD. Breakthroughs in Art, 1900–1960 takes a fresh look at the Hamburger Kunsthalle’s Modernism Collection, one of the premier collections of modern art in Germany with more than 3,000 paintings, sculptures, photographs, prints and drawings. A selection of some 125 works – both well-known highlights and special new acquisitions – illustrate the profusion of new ideas and techniques that emerged as artists broke with tradition during six decades marked by extraordinary upheavals in culture and society. A great diversity of approaches becomes apparent within the various modernist trends. Expressionism is embodied by iconic works produced by members of artist groups such as »Die Brücke« and »Der Blaue Reiter«, and the École de Paris is represented by painters including Sonia Delaunay-Terk, Georges Braque and Pablo Picasso. Also featured are pioneers of early modernism such as Edvard Munch, Paula Modersohn-Becker, Lovis Corinth, Max Beckmann and Ani

title: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston hosts US debut exhibition of jeweler Bernhard Schobinger
summary: In September the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston presents Going Underground: The Jewels of Bernhard Schobinger, tracing the radical career of Swiss avant-garde artist Bernhard Schobinger, who has created some of the most distinctive, influential and pathbreaking jewelry of the past five decades. This is the first exhibition in the U.S. to examine Schobinger’s groundbreaking work. Going Underground features 53 pivotal pieces of experimental jewelry and select sculpture from 1968 to the present, with necklaces, bracelets, and rings drawn from prominent private collections and the holdings of the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. The installation is on view on the second floor of the Nancy and Rich Kinder Building September 3, 2026 – January 3, 2027. title: More than 130 Carl Van Vechten portraits offer a who's who of 20th century cultural leaders
summary: Between the 1930s and 1950s, hundreds of cultural luminaries from the early 20th century sat for portraits in a small studio in an apartment at 150 West 55th Street in Manhattan. In his apartment studio, American photographer Carl Van Vechten (1880-1964) photographed some of the most influential artists, writers, musicians and cultural leaders of the time. More than 130 of those photographs are now part of the Chrysler Museum of Art ’s collection. The transformative gift from the Philadelphia Museum of Art includes images of Walter P. Chrysler Jr., whose collection formed the foundation of the Museum. Before the gift, the Chrysler Museum only held one image by Van Vechten. title: Wembley Park unveils spectacular 30ft anamorphic Freddie Mercury mural
summary: Wembley Park, the world-famous north west London neighbourhood surrounding the National Stadium, has revealed a brand-new artistic tribute to one of the world’s greatest music legends, Freddie Mercury, to mark what would have been the British singer-songwriter’s 80th birthday on Saturday 5th September. The anamorphic mural, hand-sprayed and applied to vinyl, I’m Mr. Mercury, created by renowned British street artist Frank Styles, transforms Wembley Park’s Spanish Steps, the key pedestrian link between two of the UK’s most iconic live venues – Wembley Stadium and OVO Arena Wembley, formerly Wembley Arena – where band frontman Mercury performed multiple times with Queen. Taking centre stage across the Spanish Steps, the bespoke mural comprises an iconic monochromatic image of Mercury, against a vivid backdrop of colour and graphic elements inspired by his life, passions and artistic identity. title: Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden releases comprehensive museum guide
summary: The Smithsonian’s Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden has published Hirshhorn Museum: The Art Handbook, a vividly illustrated portable paperback guide to the permanent collection of the Hirshhorn, the national museum of modern and contemporary art. “We are delighted to publish this welcoming book for both fans of modern art and readers new to it,” said Melissa Chiu, director of the Hirshhorn. “The book builds on research we undertook during the pandemic, which resulted in both our scholarly collection book, Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden: The Collection, and this portable handbook.” The Art Handbook offers a concise yet deeply informed overview of one of the most significant modern and contemporary art collections in the United States, as well as the artistic movements that have given rise to its compelling treasures. Through hundreds of color and black-and-white images, the handbook traces the evolution of the collection from its Modernist foundations

title: Christie's reimagines its New York home to create ultimate auction house and visitor experience in Rockefeller Center
summary: Christie's auction house is reimagining its New York headquarters in landmark Rockefeller Center, expanding public space and further enhancing the auction house's ability to present great collections at the scale and with the flexibility and sophistication required to fully respect the vision of collectors and showcase the uniqueness of objects across all categories. Following Christie's recently renewed 25-year commitment to Rockefeller Center, a process that began 3 years ago, the 260-year-old auction house has engaged award-winning firm Practice for Architecture and Urbanism (PAU) and its founder Vishaan Chakrabarti, one of the most important creative talents in contemporary architecture, to act as lead design architect on the project. title: Hauser & Wirth Basel opens solo exhibition of Swiss artist Irène Zurkinden
summary: Hauser & Wirth Basel presents a solo exhibition dedicated to the work of Swiss artist Irène Zurkinden (1909 – 1987). Known for her commissioned portraits of Basel society, this presentation highlights a more intimate body of portraits and self-portraits, offering a deeply personal perspective on Zurkinden’s life. Spanning the early 1930s to the 1980s, the exhibition brings together paintings and works on paper that reveal the duality at the heart of the artist’s career. Born in Basel in 1909, Zurkinden initially trained to become a fashion illustrator, before moving to Paris in 1929 to study at the Académie de la Grande Chaumière. There, she embraced the city’s liberated culture and became a part of its vibrant artistic milieu, cultivating a social circle that included Salvador Dalí, Man Ray and Kiki de Montparnasse. title: Jennifer Guidi debuts new nature-inspired abstract paintings at Gagosian Paris
summary: Gagosian announces Waterfall, an exhibition of new works by Jennifer Guidi opening on September 3 at the rue de Ponthieu gallery in Paris. Guidi draws inspiration for this body of work from places she has experienced and imagined, expressing her meditations on the natural world and inner landscapes through vibrant colors and forms. She abstracts the elemental structures of nature to envision the convergence of the distinct yet interconnected forces that shape its features. The radiant sun or moon centered in her paintings illuminates shorelines and beaches, gentle hills and soaring mountain ranges, placid oceans and cascading waterfalls. “We can all relate to the feeling of being in nature,” Guidi notes, “walking on the beach, looking at a sunset, and knowing that this world is much larger than we are. title: Remi Guillemin appointed Global Head of Watches for Christie's
summary: Christie's announced the appointment of Remi Guillemin as Global Head of Watches, based in Geneva. With more than a decade of international experience at Christie's, Guillemin will lead the company's global Watch business across both auction and Private Sales. In his new role, Remi will oversee an international team of specialists and work closely with collectors and clients around the world to bring the most exceptional and historically significant timepieces to market. “The new global structure reinforces Christie's commitment to delivering an increasingly connected and client focused experience for the international watch collecting community. title: Monet and Renoir masterpieces lead landmark Durand-Ruel sale at Christie's Paris
summary: On 22 and 23 October, during Paris Art Week, Christie's will present the sale Durand-Ruel. Generations of Vision, an exceptional group of 62 works that have remained in the family of Paul Durand-Ruel until today. Durand-Ruel, the legendary art dealer who played a decisive historical role in the emergence and recognition of Impressionism, remains, more than a century after his death, one of the most respected figures in the history of twentieth-century art. The works that passed through his hands now hang in the world's leading museums and are among the most sought-after highlights of any exhibition devoted to Impressionism. A landmark event of the Paris season, the sale brings together major works by Claude Monet, Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Camille Pissarro, Eugène Boudin, and Alfred Sisley, as well as works by artists championed

title: Artcurial to auction 17,000 bottles from Les Climats restaurant cellar in Paris
summary: From October 2026, Artcurial will present The Cellar of Les Climats restaurant, Paris, through a series of dedicated auctions. Assembled with passion between 2013 and 2023 by Carole Colin and Denis Jamet, this outstanding cellar is renowned for the richness and quality of its Burgundy wines, offering a remarkable overview of the region’s celebrated climats. From regional appellations to Grand Crus, the auctions will feature more than 17,000 bottles across over 3,000 lots. The name of Les Climats (2013-2023) refers to Burgundy’s famous climats: precisely defined vineyard plots that shape the very identity of the region’s wine region and have been listed as a UNESCO World Heritage List since 2015. Reflecting this remarkable mosaic of terroirs, Les Climats wine cellar brings together all the region’s major appellations. title: MoMA's 18th Annual Film Benefit to honor Steven Spielberg
summary: The Museum of Modern Art’s 2026 Film Benefit, presented by CHANEL, will honor Academy Award–winning director and producer Steven Spielberg on November 12. Spielberg is one of the most successful and influential filmmakers in history, having directed more than 35 feature films and earned three Academy Awards and a record nine nominations for Best Director, including wins for Schindler’s List (1993) and Saving Private Ryan (1998). As a producer, he holds the record for the most Best Picture nominations at 14 total, including a win for Schindler’s List. For over 50 years his films—including Lincoln (2012), Bridge of Spies (2015), The Post (2017), West Side Story (2021), and The Fabelmans (2022)—have generated multiple Academy Award nominations. title: Galerie Miranda opens fall season with Justine Kurland and Mariah Robertson exhibition
summary: To open its 2026 fall season, Galerie Miranda presents a two-person exhibition by contemporary artists Justine Kurland (1969, American) and Mariah Robertson (1975, American), both known for challenging the photographic status quo. In the exhibition Antiphoto, Justine Kurland and Mariah Robertson do not just challenge the photographic canon, they lay it to siege, by cutting up, painting over, photocopying and repurposing its founding pillars. Justine Kurland contributes two distinct bodies of work to the exhibition. 99 Nudes on the Wall (2026) is a collage in ninety-nine parts. Installed as a sprawling mural, it evolves in real time as transactions are made: Individual works are removed upon purchase, generating dynamic compositions that reflect the demands of the market. title: New National Air and Space Museum video series brings aerospace learning into classrooms
summary: The Smithsonian’s National Air and Space Museum has launched “On Air,” a new educational video series for a middle school audience. “On Air” consists of short classroom-friendly videos, developed for grades five through eight, that introduce students to artifacts and stories from the museum’s collection and exhibitions. The videos align with national standards and include additional resources for teachers to incorporate them into their classrooms. Each month of the school year, the museum will release a collection of videos focused on a specific topic. Every collection contains four videos under 10 minutes in length and an accompanying educator guide featuring classroom resources, student activities and full lesson plans. title: Chef DeVonn Francis to open new café at MoMA PS1 this fall
summary: This fall, MoMA PS1 will open Symone, a new café by acclaimed chef and culinary tastemaker DeVonn Francis. Inspired by French-African cuisine and guided by seasonal ingredients, Symone marks Francis’s first restaurant and will offer a daytime dining experience that brings together food, art, and creative communities. In advance of the café opening in early October, Francis will offer a preview of select menu items from Symone at Printed Matter’s NY Art Book Fair from September 24 to 27, 2026. With free admission to MoMA PS1 for all visitors, Symone will be fully accessible during museum hours, welcoming visitors and neighbors to gather, dine, and connect. title: Sakshi Gallery presents Pallavi Singh's solo exhibition The Familiar
summary: Marking Pallavi Singh’s first solo with Sakshi Gallery, The Familiar brings together a body of paintings that explores how images and objects become connected to ideas of gender and identity. Singh draws attention to details that might otherwise go unnoticed, revealing how associations of gender can be embedded within the way we look at images. The initial ideas for these works took shape during Singh’s time at the Jan van Eyck Academie, where she began looking closely at the ways language and gender are connected. Language is an important starting point for Singh’s practice. Her interest lies in the ways ordinary objects are assigned gender through language, and how these associations shift across cultures and contexts. title: Polish artist Krzysztof Grzybacz presents new body-focused paintings at Pace
summary: Pace will present Haruspex, a solo exhibition of new paintings by Kraków-based artist Krzysztof Grzybacz, at its London gallery beginning September 3, 2026. Marking the artist's first solo exhibition in the UK, the presentation will feature new work that explores the body as a construct, how it holds memories of past selves, and how those selves remain visible as we age. Known for his exploration of the relationship between everyday objects, the human body, and nature, Grzybacz shifts his focus in Haruspex to the body as a site where memory, instinct, and lived experience accumulate in layers. Drawing together studio sketches and fragments of thought and the subconscious, he creates paintings that stand alone rather than forming a linear narrative. title: UC Santa Barbara museum to celebrate David Gebhard centennial in 2027
summary: In 2027, The Art, Design & Architecture Museum at the University of California, Santa Barbara, will celebrate the centennial of David Gebhard (1927–1996), renowned architectural historian, professor, museum director, preservation advocate, and founder of the Museum’s prestigious Architecture and Design Collection. Through a year-long program of events, Gebhard will be honored for his extraordinary contributions to the study, documentation, and preservation of historic and modern architecture, with particular emphasis on Southern California. title: Large-scale contemporary Greek art exhibition Always the Sun to open in Riga
summary: The exhibition ALWAYS THE SUN, curated by Marina Fokidis, brings together a constellation of 27 Greek artists whose practices are shaped by the interplay of geography, light, climate, and cultural legacy. It is the first large-scale presentation of contemporary Greek art in the Baltic region. Drawing inspiration from the song by The Stranglers, the exhibition approaches the sun not as a motif, but as a medium of thought, perception, and lived experience. It explores how the brightness, heat, and exposure of the Mediterranean have influenced aesthetic languages and fostered strategies of survival, intimacy, and adaptation. The curator Marina Fokidis emphasizes: “The sun. title: Royal College of Art reveals winners of 2026 Hyundai Motor Group Awards
summary: The Royal College of Art (RCA) has today unveiled the winners of the Hyundai Motor Group Awards for Excellence in Sustainability and Creative Practice 2026. Now in their fourth year, the annual awards champion outstanding work from across the RCA’s diverse art and design disciplines. The initiative highlights the critical role interdisciplinary perspectives play in addressing complex global challenges, celebrating projects that challenge societal norms, propose tangible solutions, or evoke powerful responses to the climate crisis. Members of the 2026 graduating cohort were invited to submit visionary works across three distinct categories: Inspiration, Innovation, and Aesthetics & Craft. title: Kunsthalle Friart Fribourg to present Mira M. Yang exhibition
summary: Mira M. Yang develops work that engages with cultural transfer, memory, and belonging from a diasporic perspective. It emanates from something performative or staged, which holds the image of a transmission. To perform, in this sense, means to transmit signals, energies, and affects. It is often a performing body that acts as the transceiver, although more recently M. Yang has also used animated sculptures made from machine parts as surrogates for absent human bodies. For the exhibition Ensemble, which will be presented in two chapters at the Kunsthalle Friart Fribourg and the Fondation Pernod Ricard in Paris, M. Yang has developed new sound assemblages and a film, which are being shown in varying configurations. title: The Renaissance Society presents Karimah Ashadu: Tendered
summary: The Renaissance Society and Fondazione In Between Art Film present Tendered, a solo exhibition by Karimah Ashadu, whose moving-image practice examines the conditions under which bodies are rendered legible within contemporary systems of labor and value, especially within the cultural context of Nigeria and its diaspora. Karimah Ashadu: Tendered will be on view at the Renaissance Society in Chicago from September 12–November 1, 2026. Working across film and installation, Ashadu develops close, sustained encounters with people whose lives unfold within informal economies, attending to how aspirations are negotiated under material constraint. The exhibition marks the U.S. debut of MUSCLE, a new moving image installation co-commissioned and co-produced by the Renaissance Society, Fondazione In Between

title: Group exhibition at Frac Lorraine explores Polish identity and migration histories
summary: The exhibition challenges the myth of a homogeneous national storyline to address the diversity that constitutes a culture’s various layers. By focusing on the migratory movements that have shaped Poland’s culture, while tracing connections to Lorraine, it reveals forgotten chapters of the its history. The works showcase the extent to which this country—which often casts itself as a homogeneous nation—contains a multitude of parallel histories, including those of the social and cultural minorities that constitute it. Echoing the ties of the artists with Poland—whether through residence, birth, or family roots—coexisting histories connected through diasporic links continue to shape this complex and rich geographical area. title: Economies of Deferral exhibition explores New Zealand energy industry and labor
summary: Economies of Deferral tells a story of development and abandonment from within the heart of Aotearoa New Zealand’s energy industry. The exhibition includes artists from Taranaki, Aotearoa and working internationally between the 1980s to the present whose work bears witness to, advocates from within, and troubles our understanding of the profound economic, social and political transformations that have shaped the last four decades. At the project’s heart is a re-engagement with Urenui-born film- and video-maker Darcy Lange’s 1987 video Lack of Hope: Co-op a new future, produced in collaboration with John Miller (Ngāi Tawake ki te Tuawhenua, Ngāti Rēhia, Te Whiu, Ngāpuhi).
